findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.comment: Signed employee reporting agreements are not available on file at the facility. Education was conducted and blank copies in English were provided to PIC. Inspectors will drop off agreements in Chinese early next week. Follow up scheduled for Monday September 28, 2026. Ensure that all employees sign a health reporting agreement and keep them available for all future inspections.
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A). [Pf[

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed the handwashing sink to not have soap available. There was two bottles of hand sanitizer near the handwashing sink. PIC was made aware and corrected the violation by providing soap for the handwashing sink. Ensure that all handwashing sinks are stocked with soap at all times of food preparation and hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: (2nd REPEAT) Inspector observed foods improperly stored in several locations: 1) carrots stored in a cardboard box that previously contained frozen chicken. CORRECTED- Carrots were removed from the box. Store vegetables in their receiving boxes, in plastic containers, or directly on shelves. 2) Packages of raw pork observed above clams and seafood in the long open air cooler. CORRECTED: Pork was moved to store elsewhere in the cooler. 3) A bag of raw chicken observed stored above vegetables in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- Chicken was moved to storage below vegetables and other animal proteins. Ensure foods are stored to prevent cross contamination. Store raw animal proteins in relation to their cooking temperatures.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas. [P]

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed there to be no stem thermometers available at the facility. PIC was made aware that probe thermometers are required to monitor temperatures of food being stored at the facility. Follow up scheduled for Monday September 28, 2026. Ensure that a food temperature measuring device is always available at the facility.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.comment:
Several items were observed without complete labeling. 1) Pitted haw (fruit) and tofu observed without any labeling. Ensure that prepackaged foods are labeled to indicate their contents and source. 2) Tofu and lo mein noodles observed without ingredient labeling. Label foods with their ingredients, or keep an ingredient binder with labels upon customer request. 3) Several animal proteins (shrimp, etc) observed without cooking instructions on packaging or posted nearby. Add safe cooking instruction to labels or post signage near all raw animal proteins with safe cooking instructions.
3-602.11(B)(1)-(4) and (6) Food Labels. (B) Label information shall include: (1) The common name of the FOOD, or absent a common name, an adequately descriptive identity statement; (2) If made from two or more ingredients, a list of ingredients and subingredients in descending order of predominance by weight, including a declaration of artificial colors, artificial flavors and chemical preservatives, if contained in the FOOD; (3) An accurate declaration of the net quantity of contents; (4) The name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor; and (6) Except as exempted in the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act § 403(q)(3) - (5), nutrition labeling as specified in 21 CFR 101 - Food Labeling and 9 CFR 317 Subpart B Nutrition Labeling. [C]

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
findings.comment: Several knives were observed stored in the gap between prep counters. CORRECTED- Knives were removed to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized. Store knives on a clean surface, rather than between tables which is not easily cleanable or regularly sanitized.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12(C) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(C) On a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food-contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency specified under §§ 4-602.11 and 4-702.11.[C]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspector observed raw chicken feet being stored over raw beef in the WIC. Discussed with PIC, and PIC moved the chicken below the beef. Ensure that meats are stored in the correct order to prevent contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Two workers were observed to not have food handler certifications. Discussed with PIC and PIC stated they would get them soon. Ensure all people handling food in establishment are licensed. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Required records available: shellstock tags, parasite destruction
findings.comment:
3-202.18: Inspector observed no shell stock tags on clams. Educated PIC on proper retention of shell stock tags from distributor. Ensure that all shell stock tags are kept for 90 days after the sale of the last unit item. Ensure that bags are not mixed as well; keep items in the bag they came in.

(A) Shellstock shall come in harvester/dealer-identified containers and shall include: harvester’s ID #, date of harvest, harvest location, type and quantity of shellfish, and “THIS tag is required to be attached until container is empty or retagged and thereafter kept on file for 90days.” (Pf) (B)  Subject to embargo if label is incomplete (C). (C) Dealer shall be listed before Harvester (C).

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: Inspector observed raw meat and eggs being stored over seafood and produce. Educated PIC on proper storage order (TOP->BOTTOM: Fish, Beef & Pork, Eggs, Poultry). Ensure all foods are stored in proper order to minimize cross-contamination potential.

(A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P).

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: Inspector observed several packages of chilis, herbs, and peeled garlic to not have date marks on them. Educated PIC on proper date marking of store-packed produce. Ensure all food items packed in store have a date mark on them.

(A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf).

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container
findings.comment:
3-601.11: Inspector observed multiple items with improper labeling. Educated PIC on importance of labeling every house-packed item properly. Ensure all house-packed meats include cooking instructions. Ensure all vegetable are labeled with the common name. Ensure all items removed from original packaging have labels available for customer viewing. Discussed posting labels/names/cooking instructions on the outside of respective coolers and freezers.

PACKAGED FOOD shall comply with standard of identity requirements in 21 CFR 131-169 and 9 CFR 319 Definitions and standards of identity or composition, and the general requirements in 21 CFR 130  Food Standards: General and 9 CFR 319 Subpart A  General.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
3-305.11: Inspector observed several boxes on the floor of the facility in dry storage as well as walk-in coolers. Educated PIC on importance of keeping food 6 inches off of the floor. Ensure that all stored food and food items are kept 6 inches or more off of the floor.

(A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
Foods were observed thawing in the sink without running water. Discussed with PIC.  Ensure foods being thawed in the sink are completely submerged with running water to prevent contamination.

3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container
findings.comment:
Foods separated and packaged at the facility were observed without a label.  Discussed with PIC, who pulled the packages off the self for labeling.  Ensure when repackaging foods, the packages are properly labeled.

3-602.11: (A) FOOD PACKAGED in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be properly labeled. (B) Regulatory requirements-(1) The common name of the FOOD/identity statement; 106 (2) List ingredients in descending order of predominance by weight, declaration of artificial colors and flavors and chemical preservatives; (3) net contents; (4) The name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor; and (5) MAJOR FOOD ALLERGENS. Pf (6) Nutrition labeling as specified in 21 CFR 101 - Food Labeling and 9 CFR 317 Subpart B Nutrition Labeling UNLESS EXEMPT Under FDCA. (Pf) (C) Bulk FOOD for CONSUMER self-dispensing shall be labeled in plain view. (D) Bulk, unPACKAGED FOODS portioned for CONSUMERS shall be properly labeled.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
No sanitizer bucket was made upon inspector arrival.  Discussed with PIC, a sanitizer bucket was made during inspection.  Ensure a sanitizer bucket is made and available while repackaging food.

4-602.11: (A) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned before each use, each time there is a change in work, between uses of raw FOODS to RTE FOODS, before using FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE, and when contamination has occurred. (C) Cleaned at least every 4 hours.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
Chlorine test strips were not present at time if inspection.  Discussed with PIC.  Ensure test strips are available at facility.

4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
-Walk-in cooler fan was observed to contain an accumulation of dust.  Equipment shall be cleaned at a frequency to preclude accumulation of dust.  Ensure the walk-in cooler and freezer fans and grates are cleaned regularly.
-Mold was observed along the top of the mop sink.  Ensure this area is cleaned regularly to prevent an accumulation of mold.

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Caulk around bathroom sinks in both the men’s and women’s bathrooms has cracked and separated the sink and wall.  Areas subject to moisture must be easily cleanable and non-absorbent.  Ensure caulk is repaired by next routine inspection.

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
The complaint was concerning soft food in the freezer. The complaint does not say what type of food was soft. During inspection the employee stated that they cut meat and put it into the freezer. They have freshly cut meat in the freezer that is not yet completely frozen. This is a likely explanation of the complaint. The temperature of this meet is 28F.  Other foods in the freezers were frozen solid. The manager stated that the freezers had gone down yesterday (2.24.22). The manager stated that when they noticed the wall freezers going down they moved the new chest freezers from their storage to the facility and moved the frozen items into the individual chest style freezers. They had recently purchased the new bank of freezers for the grocery but had not yet put them into use. According to the refrigeration technician, the entire building had a single unit that controlled all of the coolers and freezers in the market. He said that they would be back Monday (2.28.22) to start work on the job and that it may take a week and a half in order to repair the unit and get the coolers and freezers up and running again. They did get one refrigeration unit working today. This unit is holding at 40F according to the independent thermometer. The staff began to stock this unit with bean sprouts and other tofu products which were observed to be on the open shelves in the facility upon arrival. Some of the other keep refrigerated items were kept in the walk in cooler according to the staff. This walk in has an integrated thermometer which was reading 45F. These bean sprouts along with the other items labeled keep refrigerated are observed to be above 41F and have been for an undetermined amount of time. We placed the tofu, egg products and noodle products into boxes to move to the back room. Several boxes of items were discarded before we could embargo them. The remaining foods have been embargoed and will be further researched in order to determine if the foods can be kept or if they will be discarded.

 3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Food obtained from approved source
findings.comment:
3-201.11: Upon arrival, inspector discovered facility receives bulk meat and produce from supplier in Chicago, and repackages it for individual sale at the market. Discussed with PIC limits of current permit classification, class III, implies no food handling whatsoever. Facility advised to contact SCPDH and set up a pre-opening where food director will confirm facilities are adequate to operate as class II. For time being, PIC advised to halt food preparation until meeting occurs. 

See general comments, SCDPH has upgraded facility to a class II as of 9/13 and may now continue this behavior. No further action.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. 

Handwashing sink filled with dirty dishes. Discussed with PIC. Ensure handwashing sink is available at all times for employee use.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

Observed staff conducting cleaning, pest control, opening the doors, stocking shelves, while wearing the same pair of gloves. Discussed with PIC. Gloves are single use only and must be changed, and handwash conducted, when contaminated. COS.

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.citation_text:
3-301.11 (P) Food employee used bare hands to handle ready to eat foods. Food employees shall use suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas/tongs, dispensing equipment or single use gloves when handling ready to eat foods. Reference 3-301.11.
Observed employee handling produce with bare hands in the stock area of the store. Ensure employees are gloved properly when handling ready to eat foods. Change gloves in between tasks and wash hands frequently and in between glove changes. Manager found gloves for employees to use.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.citation_text:
3-305.11  (C) Food stored in an unapproved location **** . Food shall be protected by contamination by storing it: 1) in a clean, dry location; 2) where it is not exposed to splash, dust or other contamination; 3) at least 6 inches above the floor. Reference 3-305.11.
Observed a container of Jellyfish uncovered and on the floor near the produce section. 
Additionally observed a container of chicken feet and a container of leeks on floor of walk-in cooler. Manager removed products from floor and covered them appropriately to prevent contamination.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-302.14  (Pf) Test kits or other devices are not available to the employees to measure sanitizing solution concentration. Provide a test kit or other measuring device so the employees can measure concentrations and ensure proper sanitization. Avoid a concentration of sanitizer that is too high, which can be toxic. Reference 4-302.14.
Facility does not have test strips for bleach. Manager will contact GFS to purchase test kits for sanitizers.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
REPEAT: Observed boxes of pork stored on the floor in the walk-in freezer. Store all food at least six inches off the floor.
750-130(b) Food shall be stored at least 6 inches off the floor.  Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
CORRECTED: Observed sleeves of single service trays stored with the food contact surface exposed. Store all single service items in a manner to protect the food contact surface from being contaminated. The single service trays were properly stored during the routine inspection to correct the violation.
750-880 Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user.

findings.title: Containers covered, adequate number, insect and rodent proof, emptied at proper intervals, clean
findings.comment:
Observed the outside dumpster to be open upon the inspector arrival. Close the outside dumpster when not be used to prevent rodents.
750-1130a Garbage and refuse shall be kept in durable easily cleanable, insect-proof, and rodent-proof containers.
